pairs.question: Noster es an adversariorum?
pairs.answer: Nequaquam, sed sum princeps exercitus Domini et nunc venio.
pairs.derivation: Joshua addresses the man with the drawn sword. Dropped the narrative frame 'cum autem esset Iosue... perrexitque ad eum et ait'; the bare alternative question (an...) is self-contained. Answer drops the speech tag 'qui respondit'; the reply directly answers and is complete at the first full stop.

pairs.question: Quid dominus meus loquitur ad servum suum?
pairs.answer: Solve calciamentum de pedibus tuis, locus enim in quo stas sanctus est.
pairs.derivation: Joshua's question to the prince of the Lord's host. Dropped the frame 'cecidit Iosue pronus... et adorans ait'. Answer drops 'inquit' and stops at the first full stop, cutting the following narration 'fecitque Iosue ut sibi fuerat imperatum'.

pairs.question: Quinam estis et unde venistis?
pairs.answer: De terra longinqua valde venerunt servi tui in nomine Domini Dei tui.
pairs.derivation: Joshua questions the Gibeonites. Dropped 'quibus Iosue ... ait'. Answer drops 'responderunt' and stops after the clause answering who/whence, cutting the digression 'audivimus enim famam potentiae eius...'.

pairs.question: Cur nos decipere fraude voluistis, ut diceretis procul valde habitamus a vobis, cum in medio nostri sitis?
pairs.answer: Nuntiatum est nobis servis tuis quae promisisset Dominus Deus tuus Mosi servo suo ut traderet vobis omnem terram et disperderet cunctos habitatores eius timuimus igitur valde et providimus animabus nostris vestro terrore conpulsi et hoc consilium inivimus.
pairs.derivation: Joshua's 'cur' question (v.22) is answered in v.24, skipping v.23 which is Joshua continuing to pronounce the curse, not the Gibeonites' reply. Question drops 'vocavit Gabaonitas Iosue et dixit eis'; answer drops 'qui responderunt'. The whole verse-sentence is the genuine answer (they acted out of fear), so kept contiguous through 'et hoc consilium inivimus'.

pairs.question: Quid habes?
pairs.answer: Da mihi benedictionem: terram australem et arentem dedisti mihi, iunge et inriguam.
pairs.derivation: Caleb asks his daughter Axah. Dropped the frame 'cui Chaleb ... inquit'. Answer drops 'at illa respondit' and stops before the narration 'dedit itaque ei Chaleb inriguum superius et inferius'.

pairs.question: Quare dedisti mihi possessionem sortis et funiculi unius, cum sim tantae multitudinis et benedixerit mihi Dominus?
pairs.answer: Si populus multus es, ascende in silvam et succide tibi spatia in terra Ferezei et Rafaim, quia angusta est tibi possessio montis Ephraim.
pairs.derivation: The sons of Joseph complain in one interrogative speech (quare); Joshua answers directly. Question drops 'locutique sunt filii Ioseph ad Iosue atque dixerunt'; answer drops 'ad quos Iosue ait'. The full reply answers the complaint (go clear more land since you are many) and is kept whole.
